messages:
kevin: Heads-up — customer reported lost audit events after we flipped on HEC batching + KMS-signed webhook delivery this morning. They see gaps in Splunk and some empty objects in the S3 fallback.

liza: oh no. which flow? webhook primary -> splunk HEC, fallback -> s3 export?

kevin: yep. primary is HEC batch endpoint. when batch size hits ~1200 events we send a single multi-event payload. Splunk shows partial ingestion and the S3 manifest has zero-length parts for some batches.

sam: do we have any errors in delivery logs? dlq entries?

kevin: there are transient 400/415 responses from customer HEC proxy, and our delivery worker logs show "write failed: EPIPE" for one connection. no DLQ for those — they were retried and then we fell back to S3 partial upload.

maria: could be newline-delimited JSON boundary issues combined with KMS signature verification. If signing happens on the whole batch but intermediary proxies chunk the body, recipient might verify incremental chunks incorrectly.

security-eng: agree. Splunk HEC expects event-per-line or simple JSON array depending on config. If a proxy uses chunked transfer and verifies per-chunk signature headers, signature will mismatch.

kevin: here's an example of the headers we send: 
```
POST /services/collector/event/1.0 HTTP/1.1
Host: splunk-acme.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 123456
X-Redwood-KeyId: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd
X-Redwood-KMS-Signature: Base64Signature==
X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key: 79a4e2

{...NDJSON batch ...}
```

liza: if proxies convert to chunked or inject gzip, Content-Length may be removed or changed. KMS signature must be computed over canonicalized bytes. We currently sign raw body bytes and put signature header. Any middleware that modifies body invalidates sig.

sam: action items to triage: 1) add body-hash header (sha256) we can recompute on receiver side for debugging 2) make batch upload safer — prefer smaller batch_size for new customers behind proxies 3) detect chunked transfer and treat signature as not verifiable and fallback w/ additional metadata.

maria: +1. For #1 we can add: `X-Redwood-Body-SHA256: hexsha` (debug-only for now). For #2 proposed default for splunk-hec behind proxies = 200 events or 256KB. For #3 fallback behavior should record reason code in S3 manifest.

kevin: customer onboarding note: when we enable KMS-signed webhooks we should add a compatibility checklist for their proxies (allow raw content-length, don't re-encode, allow our signature header). link to spec: https://redwood.internal/docs/audit-delivery/webhooks#signing

security-eng: also surface an evaluation flag in Console per-tenant: "verify-splunk-signature" with telemetry. That way we can see how many verify failures happen during ramp.

audit-bot: deploy triggered by sam:patch/add-debug-body-hash 1763457200

sam: quick debug snippet we pushed to workers: 
```python
# compute canonical sha256 and sign with KMS
body = b"\n".join(lines)
sha = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
sig = kms_client.sign(KeyId=key_id, Message=body, SigningAlgorithm='RSASSA_PSS_SHA_256')
headers['X-Redwood-Body-SHA256'] = sha
headers['X-Redwood-KMS-Signature'] = base64.b64encode(sig['Signature']).decode()
```

maria: also adding handling when S3 fallback objects are zero-length: add object-level metadata `x-redwood-delivery-error: partial-batch-chunked` and include `original_batch_size` + `event_count_sent`.

kevin: good. for customer support we should send a sample reconciliation script so they can match what we attempted to send vs what Splunk ingested. small jq example: 
```bash
# reconstruct NDJSON bodies from S3 manifest and count lines
aws s3 cp s3://acme-backups/2026-03-05/batch-123.ndjson - | wc -l
```

liza: policy note: update onboarding doc to call out proxies and gzip/chunked edge cases. Also add a short checklist for SIEM teams to accept Redwood KMS-signed headers.

kevin: question — should we change to signing per-event instead of per-batch for better compatibility? trade-offs: more KMS calls, higher cost, but more granular verification and reduces chunking risk.

security-eng: per-event signing is safer but we can do hybrid: split large batches into signed sub-batches of ~200 events server-side before signing. That keeps KMS overhead reasonable and avoids chunking mismatches.

sam: I'll implement sub-batching + debug body-hash and add manifest metadata keys. Also add additional retry logic for 415/4xx that records response body for support.

maria: FYI I've updated the audit schema docs to include `delivery.problem_code` enum with `partial_batch_chunked`, `kms_sig_mismatch`, `hec_bad_request`.

kevin: perfect. i'll draft a short customer-facing explanation and include mitigation steps they can take on their proxy. will ping @maria for doc link when ready.

security-eng: cool. timeline?

sam: aiming to roll debug flag + sub-batching in canary tomorrow 09:00 PT, broader rollout after 24h of metrics.

kevin: thanks team. i'll open a support ticket template and attach the recon steps. :thumbsup:
